newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crude holds steady through hectic day's trade.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crude holds steady through hectic day's trade.

text.p: Values for wet Brent and other North Sea crudes appeared little changed when the dust settled after a flurry of physical deals on Monday, traders said.
"A lot has been done but I wouldn't say the market has moved sharply in either direction," said one dealer.

Five Brent cargoes were reported traded. A Jan 28-30 cargo was bought by a U.S. trader at Feb Brent -15 cents, a Feb 3-5 cargo fetched Feb Brent -20 cents, and a Feb 1-3 was done at March Brent +13 cents. An end-Jan and a Feb 2-4 cargo were traded at prices tied to Dated Brent quotes.
No clear direction was offered by today's Brent dates.
Of the two turning wet on Monday one was kept by Wall Street trader JP Morgan while the other was clocked to Mobil.

Differentials for other North Sea grades held steady, with a Forties loading Feb 5-7 traded at Dated Brent +28 cents and two early-Feb Osebergs sold at Dated +32 cents. A Feb 9-11 Statfjord fetched Dated Brent +37 cents, while another was heard done at a p+c price.
"You'll notice that not much of the buying is from refiners," a trader said.
Dealers said that poor refining margins were being countered by the expected exit of North Sea barrels from the region.
A Wall Street trader was heard to have buying commitments for Brent cargoes into the U.S. Gulf Coast for Feb 20-25 delivery.
On paper, Brent intermonth spreads were steady to slightly firmer with Feb/Mar talked at +29/+34 late in the day after trading at +30 cents. Mar/Apr changed hands at +43 cents.
March Brent paper was trading 16 cents up at around $22.70 a barrel in line with IPE screen levels at 1845 GMT.
CFDs clawed back earlier losses with next week's dates traded at March +13 cents, the same level at an earlier wet Brent trade.
